name: Aljazira Bank (formerly Bank AlJazira)
legal_name: aljazira bank (a Saudi Joint Stock Company); trading name until the Dec 2025 rebrand: Bank AlJazira
founded: 1975 (Royal Decree 46/M dated 21 Jun 1975); began business 9 Oct 1976 by taking over the Saudi branches of the National Bank of Pakistan (CR 4030010523 dated 27 Jul 1976, Jeddah). Listed on Tadawul.
ownership_summary: Widely held Tadawul-listed bank with issued capital of SAR 12,812.5m (1,281.25m shares of SAR 10). Two holders are disclosed above 5% at 31 Dec 2025 in the 2025 Board report: Mr. Ibrahim Abdulrahman Mohammed Al Qunaibet (77,734,378 shares) and Consolidated Brothers Development Company (64,063,743 shares). Percentages are computed from the share count. Bonus shares were issued during 2025 (EPS restated).

shareholders.holder: Mr. Ibrahim Abdulrahman Mohammed Al Qunaibet

government_link: None found. No government entity appears among holders above 5% in the 2025 Board report (S5). Holdings below 5% were not checked.
group_structure: Parent bank with 100%-owned subsidiaries: AlJazira Capital Company (CMA-licensed brokerage, margin finance, asset and wealth management, investment banking, custody; profiled separately as sa-aljazira-capital), Aman Development and Real Estate Investment Company (holds real estate collateral), AlJazira Securities Limited (Cayman; Shariah-compliant derivative and capital-market transactions) and BAJ Sukuk Tier 1 Limited (Cayman; Tier 1 sukuk trustee). Associate: Aljazira Takaful Ta'awuni (33.08%: bank 29.36% plus AlJazira Capital 3.72%). The Fawri remittance business (24 centres) is run by the bank under its own brand. Double counting: AlJazira Capital's assets, revenue and AUM are consolidated in the bank's 'Brokerage and asset management' segment. Do not add sa-aljazira-capital metrics to this record.

subsidiaries.name: AlJazira Capital Company
subsidiaries.activity: Brokerage, margin financing, asset and wealth management, investment banking, custody (CMA licence 07076-37)

subsidiaries.name: Aman Development and Real Estate Investment Company
subsidiaries.activity: Holding and managing real estate collaterals on behalf of the bank

subsidiaries.name: BAJ Sukuk Tier 1 Limited (Cayman Islands)
subsidiaries.activity: Trustee for issuance of Tier 1 sukuk certificates

footprint: Saudi Arabia only (no branches abroad). 73 branches and 24 Fawri remittance centres at 30 Jun 2026 (S3 note 1). 565 ATMs and 26,249 POS terminals at end-2025 (S5). 3 Private Banking and Wealth Management centres in Riyadh, Jeddah and Al Khobar (S5). Head office: Al-Shatea District, Jeddah (S3 note 1); results releases are datelined Riyadh.
customer_segments: Personal banking (mass retail; the Premium and Wealth affluent tiers; Private Banking and Wealth Management for high-net-worth individuals), corporate and institutional banking (large and mid corporates, public sector), MSME (Aljazira Business), treasury, and remittances (Fawri). Strategic aim: 'bank of choice for affluent individuals, corporates, and institutions' (S6, S9).
business_lines: Four reportable segments (S3 note 16): Personal banking; Corporate banking; Treasury; Brokerage and asset management (AlJazira Capital). H1 2026 total operating income by segment (SAR '000): personal 1,165,057; corporate 724,724; treasury 328,063; brokerage and asset management 257,818; others and eliminations (107,506); total 2,368,156 (S3 note 16). FY2025: personal 2,328,650; corporate 1,343,154; treasury 511,747; brokerage and asset management 629,301; others (348,518); total 4,464,334 (S5). Fee and other income was 30% of H1 2026 operating income (S6). On the Q2-26 call mutual funds and trade finance together made up about 68% of net fee income from banking services (S8). All products are Shariah-compliant.

capabilities.wealth_summary: Aljazira Bank is a fully Shariah-compliant Saudi bank whose strategy since the 2023 transformation is to become the 'bank of choice for affluent individuals, corporates, and institutions'. A new brand, 'Wealth Grows Here', launched in Dec 2025 and names wealth management a core pillar; the investment arm AlJazira Capital was rebranded with it. Retail runs two affluent tiers, Premium and Wealth (Q4 2025 year-on-year growth of 24.3% and 18.7%; the report does not state the measure), and a Private Banking and Wealth Management Division serving HNW clients from three centres (Riyadh, Jeddah, Al Khobar). The Division works with AlJazira Capital to offer Shariah-compliant products, including alternative-asset funds. AlJazira Capital manages SAR 28.4bn (31 Dec 2025, +20%) across 48 funds, with brokerage, discretionary and advisory services (see sa-aljazira-capital). In H1 2026 affluent customers grew 4.4% and contributed 46% of total sales (retail commentary on the Q2-26 call); mutual funds and trade finance together were about 68% of net fee income from banking services. Premium, Wealth and Private Banking entry thresholds are not published on the current website.

private_banking.detail: The Private Banking and Wealth Management Division serves high-net-worth individuals with Shariah-compliant products from 3 centres (Riyadh, Jeddah, Al Khobar). To grow wealth clients, private companies and endowments, the Division cooperated with AlJazira Capital in 2025; a number of specialised alternative-asset funds were offered to private banking clients. It sponsored a Saudi Polo Federation tournament in AlUla and hosted a client gala. Head of the Division is not named in any source found. The privatebanking.aljazirabank.com.sa site returned HTTP 503 on 12 Oct 2026.

asset_management.detail: Through AlJazira Capital (100%): AUM SAR 28.4bn at 31 Dec 2025 (SAR 23.7bn a year earlier) and 48 funds (private equity, private credit, real estate, operating leasing, local and international money markets). The bank's 'Brokerage and asset management' segment earned SAR 257.8m of operating income in H1 2026. AlJazira Capital launched four new real estate funds in H1 2026 (S8). See sa-aljazira-capital.

brokerage.detail: Through AlJazira Capital: Saudi market plus selected GCC and international markets via the 'Aljazira Tadawul' app and web platform; margin finance; phone dealing. The bank site links to it as 'Investment' (S15). See sa-aljazira-capital.

digital_investing.detail: Bank app (ajb app; in-house design, 4.8 on Google Play and 4.7 on Apple at end-2025 per the 2025 Board report) offers a digitally subscribed Commodities Investment Account launched in 2025 (multi-currency, no branch visit) and open-banking account aggregation. Equities, sukuk and mutual-fund subscription run in AlJazira Capital's separate 'Aljazira Tadawul' app and web platform. No in-app brokerage, model portfolios or alternatives found in the bank app; the bank's digital-banking page does not mention investing features.

advisory.detail: Dedicated relationship managers for Premium and Wealth tiers and Private Banking (S13, S5). AlJazira Capital holds a CMA advising licence and markets 'Intelligence-Led Wealth Management' with a 'Get in Touch with an Advisor' route. The Q2-26 call says AI is used in 'Support and Advisory' for learning from CRM and voice logs (support context, not investment advice).

discretionary.detail: AlJazira Capital offers discretionary portfolio management to institutions and HNW individuals (equity portfolios under Shariah guidelines and a Murabaha variant); no minimum published.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or model-portfolio product found on the bank or AlJazira Capital sites. AlJazira Capital offers a Systematic Investment Plan (from SAR 100 or USD 30 a month) into its own funds; see sa-aljazira-capital. The Q2-26 call mentions a 'GenAI and agentic AI framework' for banking, support and advisory, sales; not described as an investing product.

funds_platform.detail: In-house funds of AlJazira Capital are distributed to bank clients (mutual funds are a main fee line, S8). Fund categories on the AlJazira Capital site include equity, money market, fund of funds and real estate. No third-party fund shelf or platform provider found.

structured_products.detail: Not mentioned on the bank's affluent, private banking or digital pages or in the 2025 Board report (checked 12 Oct 2026). The Cayman subsidiary AlJazira Securities Limited carries out Shariah-compliant derivative and capital-market transactions for the bank (S3 note 1); no client product is described.

private_markets.detail: AlJazira Capital alternatives: private equity, private credit, real estate and operating-leasing funds (48 funds in total). Alternative-asset funds were offered to Private Banking clients in 2025. AlJazira Capital launched the Aljazira Evergreen Private Credit Fund and a health and nutrition private equity fund in 2025 (Forbes ME).

islamic_wealth.detail: Whole franchise is Shariah-compliant under an independent Shariah Board; Shariah-compliant equity, money-market and fund-of-funds funds, sukuk trading, a Murabaha discretionary variant and Commodities Investment Account.

partners.what: Supplies funds, brokerage, custody and private-market products; Private Banking cooperates with it on alternative-asset funds; bank and AlJazira Capital contracts and dealings totalled SAR 177m in 2025

In-house platform that designs, develops and delivers customer-facing digital journeys and channels (Aljazira Mobile and Online, Fawri Mobile, Aljazira Business, AI-enabled employee app). Stated aims include reducing reliance on external vendors and recurring technology costs.
Strategic partnership for Fawri remittances reactivated in 2025; Fawri works with RIA and correspondent banks

discrepancies.detail: Statements and the Arabic and English sites now say 'aljazira bank' / 'Aljazira Bank'; older sources, third-party sites and some page titles still say 'Bank AlJazira' (the Saudi Exchange and legacy bankaljazira.com domain use the old name). The new identity launched in Dec 2025.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 'Aljazira Bank (formerly Bank AlJazira)'. Same legal entity (Royal Decree 46/M, 1975).

discrepancies.detail: The current website and 2025 Board report name two affluent tiers, Premium and Wealth. A legacy site page (seen only in search results) names ALMASI with SAR 800,000 / 400,000 / 30,000 criteria. No source links ALMASI to the Wealth tier.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded Premium and Wealth as current with no thresholds; ALMASI recorded as a legacy name of unclear status.

discrepancies.detail: The English executive page markup captions Mr. Al-Mousa's photo with another executive's name.
discrepancies.resolution: Names and titles are taken from the text list and match the Arabic page and the 2025 Board report. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: Website: 'Head of Human Capital, Corporate Strategy and Support Group'. Board report: 'Head of Human Capital and Corporate Support Group' (ownership table) and 'Head of Human Capital and Corporate Strategy and Support Group' (bio page).
Board report lists the CEO appointment as 2020; the website says board member since 2021.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded CEO appointed 2020 and board seat from 2021. Consistent with an Oct/Nov 2020 CEO start followed by election to the board.

open_items: Premium, Wealth and Private Banking eligibility thresholds are not on the current website pages checked. The ALMASI thresholds in this file come from a search snippet of a legacy page.

Head of the Private Banking and Wealth Management Division is not named in any source; the English site names no chief digital officer or head of digital. Search snippets mention a CIO (Fahad Altwaijri) and a Head of IT (Mohammed Baagiel) but these were not verified.
privatebanking.aljazirabank.com.sa returned HTTP 503 on 12 Oct 2026; re-check for eligibility, products and named staff.
Q3 2026 (30 Sep 2026) results are not yet published on the IR site (Q3 2026 links are placeholders). Re-check after late Oct 2026.
Customer, investor and employee counts are not disclosed. The full 2025 annual report PDF was not located on the IR site; the Board of Directors Report 2025 was used.
Which funds the bank app distributes, and whether any third-party funds are offered, is not documented. Commodities Investment Account details are known only from the 2025 Board report.

LinkedIn: no own-profile match found for the CEO or Head of Retail (only posts that mention them). Other executives were not checked. Search-engine checks for 2025-2026 appointments found none beyond the Jan 2025 board announcement.
Saudi Exchange (saudiexchange.sa) announcement pages were not opened; figures come from the bank's own IR documents.

Money 20/20 collaboration agreements (GO Telecom, SingleView, Bwatech) and a Diebold Nixdorf ATM software rollout were seen in search results only and are not wealth-technology relationships; not recorded as partners.
